record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Worst-case dimensions of quantum error-correcting codes
record.original_question: Let E be an e-dimensional vector space of error operators acting on an n-dimensional Hilbert space H. A quantum code C is a subspace whose projector PC satisfies PC A* B PC = lambda(A,B) PC for all A and B in E. For given e and n, find the largest dimension c(e,n) that can always be guaranteed for such a correcting code without knowing more about E, and find tough error models for which this lower bound is nearly tight.

evidence.quote: An error model E is an e-dimensional vector space of operators acting on an n-dimensional Hilbert space H. A quantum code is a subspace C ⊂ H, and is said to correct E, if the projector PC onto C satisfies PC A∗BPC = λ(A, B)PC for all A, B ∈ E, and suitable scalars λ(A, B).

• Given e and n, find the largest c = c(e, n) such that we can assert the existence of a code C of dimension c without further information about E.
• Find “tough error models” for which this bound is (nearly) tight.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space of dimension n, and let E be an e-dimensional complex vector subspace of the space of linear operators on H (an "error model"). A quantum code is a subspace C ⊆ H; let P_C denote the orthogonal projector onto C. The code C is said to correct E if there exist scalars λ(A,B) ∈ C such that
    P_C A* B P_C = λ(A,B) P_C   for all A, B ∈ E.

Define c(e,n) to be the largest integer c such that, for every e-dimensional error model E acting on an n-dimensional Hilbert space H, there exists a subspace C ⊆ H of dimension at least c which corrects E.

(a) Determine c(e,n) as a function of e and n, or give matching upper and lower bounds.
(b) Construct explicit "tough" error models E of dimension e on an n-dimensional Hilbert space for which the maximal dimension of a correcting code is (nearly) equal to c(e,n), thereby showing the lower bound is essentially tight.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source explicitly solving the worst-case guaranteed code-dimension function c(e,n) for arbitrary e-dimensional error models on an n-dimensional Hilbert space, nor exhibiting matching "tough" error models. Known results (e.g., the Knill–Laflamme conditions and Eastin–Knill theorem) provide the framework but not this specific extremal function. Current status appears not definitively settled in publicly accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: A Theory of Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (Knill–Laflamme)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the algebraic condition P_C A* B P_C = λ(A,B) P_C characterizing correctable error spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the defining condition used in the problem but does not determine the worst-case guaranteed dimension c(e,n).

status_evidence.title: Quantum error-correcting code — Error Correction Zoo
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known QECC constructions and bounds.
status_evidence.claim: No entry explicitly resolving the worst-case extremal function c(e,n) for arbitrary error subspaces.
